stem.en: With the till empty, the pipeline stalls at step one. Kabir says "so a starving cell can never restart glycolysis, because it needs coins to make coins". How do cells avoid this trap?

text.en: A cell never lets the till reach zero. It keeps a few coins in reserve and, in a pinch, uses a different molecule as a stand-in coin for the first step. The investment is small and repaid quickly. A cell that truly hit zero would be in trouble, and that is what dying is.
They do not; a starving cell dies.

feedback.en: A cell at zero ATP is dead, but a living cell is never at zero. The pipeline's first step is small enough to prime from reserves.

text.en: The first step does not really need a coin.

feedback.en: It needs one. The sim stalls without it, and so does a real cell.
Glycolysis uses no oxygen. Oxygen enters the story two modules from now.

explanation.en: Investment pipelines need a float. The cell keeps one. The danger is real, and it is why a cell out of coins is a cell out of time.
